# CellRune

> Pure Rust XLSX/XLSM reader with deterministic, explicitly scoped formula
> calculation and a package-backed round-trip document foundation. Reading and
> calculation are separate operations, macros are never executed, external
> links are never followed, and parsing, calculation, and writing costs are
> bounded.

This file is a condensed, code-accurate reference for coding agents and other
tools that add `cellrune` as a dependency. It is hand-maintained against the
`pub use` list in `crates/cellrune/src/lib.rs`; treat a mismatch with that file
as a bug in this file, not in the crate. The version described by this file is
0.1.14, uses Semantic Versioning, and requires Rust 1.88 or newer. Runnable,
task-focused patterns are shipped as `examples/` in the crate package and live
at `crates/cellrune/examples/` in the repository workspace.

## Quick start

```rust
use cellrune::{
    CalculationCellResult, CalculationOptions, ReadOptions, calculate_workbook, read_xlsx_path,
};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let workbook = read_xlsx_path("input.xlsx", ReadOptions::default())?;
    let calculation = calculate_workbook(&workbook, CalculationOptions::default());

    for (cell, result) in calculation.cells() {
        match result {
            CalculationCellResult::Value(value) => println!("{cell:?}: {value:?}"),
            CalculationCellResult::Unavailable(issue) => {
                eprintln!("{cell:?}: {}", issue.code().as_str());
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

Reading and calculation are separate calls. Reading alone never calculates a
formula; calculating never mutates the `WorkbookSnapshot` you read or the
XLSX file's own saved results. Calculation attempts every formula and returns
either a typed `CalculationCellResult::Value` or a structured
`CalculationCellResult::Unavailable` issue for each one. Independent formulas
still produce values when another formula is unavailable. Volatile functions
`TODAY()` and `NOW()` require explicit deterministic inputs through
`CalculationOptions`, or the formula reports `VolatileInputMissing` instead
of guessing.

For round-trip work, `open_xlsx_document_*` retains the exact input archive
privately and binds it to a SHA-256 `InputHash`.
`write_recalculated_xlsx_bytes`, `write_recalculated_xlsx`, and
`write_recalculated_xlsx_path` materialize a `CalculationSnapshot` made from
that exact document, preserve unrelated package content, and reopen the output
before success. The default strict policy produces no artifact if any result
is unavailable. `write_preserved_xlsx_bytes` produces an unchanged
preservation copy.

`WorkbookDraft::new()` creates a canonical XLSX workbook.
`WorkbookDraft::from_document(&XlsxDocument)` creates a preservation-backed edit
session. Effective calculation-semantic mutations advance the semantic
revision; presentation-only mutations use a separate revision, and accepted
no-ops keep the corresponding revision unchanged. Calculate `draft.workbook()`
after the final semantic edit, then call `write_xlsx_draft_bytes`,
`write_xlsx_draft`, or `write_xlsx_draft_path`.

`open_xlsx_document_*` also captures a separate `DocumentPresentation`.
It exposes shared/inline phonetic runs, explicit/effective phonetic visibility,
and default frozen panes without changing `CellValue::Text` or the calculation
fingerprint. `WorkbookDraft` provides atomic annotated-text and frozen-pane
mutations with a separate presentation revision. `PhoneticTextRange` uses
zero-based half-open UTF-16 code-unit offsets; when a range is applied to base
text, its boundaries are validated not to split a surrogate pair.
`CellPhonetics::resolved_runs` performs that translation into byte offsets, so
a consumer never writes its own UTF-16 conversion. See
`write_phonetic_workbook` and `inspect_phonetic_workbook` in the examples.

For AI hosts, the separate `cellrune-mcp` binary provides local stdio MCP
`2025-11-25` tools over `cellrune-interop::WorkbookSession`. It exposes
high-level workbook lifecycle, summary, range, usage, capability, batch edit,
recalculation, delta, and Save As operations—not one tool per spreadsheet
function. Configured filesystem roots are canonicalized at startup; every
workbook path supplied to a tool must be absolute and resolve inside one of
those roots. It has no remote transport. The 12 tools are `workbook_create`,
`workbook_open`, `workbook_close`, `workbook_summary`, `workbook_read_range`,
`workbook_function_usage`, `workbook_scan_capabilities`,
`workbook_apply_changes`, `workbook_apply_changes_v2`, `workbook_recalculate`,
`workbook_changes_since`, and `workbook_save_as`.
Read-only JSON resources expose the versioned function catalog at
`cellrune://support/functions` and active session metadata through the
`cellrune://sessions/{session_id}/summary` template. Operators can bound
resident sessions, idle lifetime, response bytes, and workbook bytes with
the corresponding `cellrune-mcp --help` options. Input validation and parsing
use the same capability-bound file handle and archive-byte ceiling. At
capacity, create/open may evict the least-recently-used idle session; active
sessions are never evicted.

The Python `Workbook` is a context manager. Python and Node.js `Workbook`
objects also expose `closed` and an idempotent `close()`. Once `close()`
returns, the binding-owned native session has been released. An active
calculation is cooperatively cancelled, and subsequent operations fail with
the stable `interop.session.closed` code.

## Naming conventions

These patterns are consistent across the entire public API. When a function
or method isn't shown in an example below, generalize from these rules rather
than guessing a name from a different XLSX crate (`calamine`,
`rust_xlsxwriter`, `umya-spreadsheet`, etc.) — their shapes do not carry over.

- **Everything public is re-exported at the crate root.** Always
  `use cellrune::X`. Internal module paths such as `cellrune::xlsx::...` or
  `cellrune::calculation::...` are private implementation detail and are never
  part of the contract.
- **Validated newtypes are constructed through `::new(...)` or a named
  variant, returning `Result<Self, ValidationError>`.** There is no public way
  to violate the constructor contract documented by that type; a file-format
  boundary can impose additional rules without tightening an existing public
  constructor in a patch release. Examples: `Row::new(u32)`,
  `Column::new(u32)`, `SheetId::new(u32)`, `FiniteNumber::new(f64)`,
  `CellAddress::from_indices(row, column)`, `CellAddress::from_a1("A1")`,
  `SheetName::new(String)`, `TableName::new(String)`,
  `TableColumnName::new(String)`, `DiagnosticCode::new(String)`,
  `SourceId::new(String)`, `FormulaText::from_xlsx(String)` /
  `FormulaText::from_user_input(String)`, `DefinedName::new(...)`,
  `ProviderIdentity::new(name, version)`, `Diagnostic::new(...)`,
  `CellRange::new(start, end)`.
- **Limit construction is family-specific:** `ReadLimits`, `WriteLimits`, and
  `CalculationLimits` start from `Default::default()` and use
  `.with_max_x(value)`, returning `ReadOptionsError`, `WriteOptionsError`, or
  `CalculationOptionsError` when a zero budget is rejected. `SessionLimits`
  uses either `Default::default()` or the five-argument
  `SessionLimits::new(...) -> Result<Self, SessionError>`, then optionally
  `.with_formula_rewrite_limits(...)` and
  `.with_table_materialization_limit(...)`. Option constructors and
  non-budget setters such as
  `ReadOptions::new`, `WriteOptions::new`,
  `RecalculationWriteOptions::new`,
  `CalculationOptions::with_today_serial`,
  `CalculationOptions::with_now_serial`, and
  `CalculationOptions::with_limits` return `Self` directly.
- **Getters are bare nouns, never `get_`-prefixed,** and are frequently
  `const fn` (`.code()`, `.severity()`, `.limits()`,
  `.max_dependency_edges()`, `.today_serial()`).
- **Public failure/value families are owned by different boundaries — never mixed:**
  see the Error taxonomy table below. Pick the family by *what layer failed*,
  not by guessing a generic `Error`/`Result` shape.
- **Public enums that may grow new variants are `#[non_exhaustive]`**
  (`CellValue`, `ExcelError`, `ValidationError`, `ValidationErrorCode`, `XlsxErrorCode`,
  `XlsxWriteErrorCode`, `ReadOptionsError`, `WriteOptionsError`,
  `CalculationOptionsError`, `CalculationIssueCode`, `SessionErrorCode`,
  `CalculationDecisionReason`, `MaterializedResultOrigin`, `FormulaDialect`,
  `FormulaMetadata`, `WorkbookChange`, `XlsxDocumentKind`,
  `RecalculationWritePolicy`, `ArithmeticSemantics`, `FinancialSolverSemantics`,
  `DefinedNameAnalysis`, `DefinedNameReferenceArea`,
  `DefinedNameDynamicKind`, `DefinedNameExternalTargetKind`,
  `DefinedNameInvalidReason`, `DefinedNameUnsupportedReason`,
  `DefinedNameAnalysisLimitKind`, `DefinedNameAnalysisErrorKind`,
  `PhoneticType`, `PhoneticAlignment`, `TableType`, `TotalsRowFunction`,
  `TableCalendarType`, `TableDateTimeGrouping`, `TableCustomFilterOperator`,
  `TableDynamicFilterType`, `TableIconSet`, `TableSortBy`, `TableSortMethod`,
  `TableFilterItem`, and `TableFilterCriteria`). A
  `match` on one of these needs a wildcard arm even if every current variant
  is handled.
- **Every stable machine code exposes `.as_str()`,** returning `&str` or
  `&'static str` for programmatic comparison and logging
  (`XlsxErrorCode::as_str`, `DiagnosticCode::as_str`,
  `CalculationIssueCode::as_str`, `ExcelError::as_str`). Never branch on the
  human-readable `Display`/message string — only on `.code()`/`.as_str()`.
- **Sheet and defined-name lookups are case-insensitive** but preserve and
  return the original spelling (`WorkbookSnapshot::sheet_by_name`,
  `DefinedName::name`).
- **Table lookup uses OOXML `displayName`, not `name`.** `displayName` is the
  workbook-global formula/UI name; `name` is the worksheet-local programmatic
  object-model name. Both preserve spelling and compare case-insensitively.
- **`CellAddress::from_a1` / `Sheet::cell_by_a1` accept only an unqualified
  A1 address** (`"A1"`, `"XFD1048576"`) — no sheet prefix, no `$` anchors.
  Those belong to formula-reference syntax, which this workbook-lookup helper
  deliberately rejects.

## Public API surface

### Entry points — reading

- `read_xlsx_path(path: impl AsRef<Path>, options: ReadOptions) -> Result<WorkbookSnapshot, XlsxReadError>`
- `read_xlsx_bytes(bytes: &[u8], options: ReadOptions) -> Result<WorkbookSnapshot, XlsxReadError>`
- `read_xlsx<R: Read + Seek>(reader: R, options: ReadOptions) -> Result<WorkbookSnapshot, XlsxReadError>`
- `inspect_package<R: Read + Seek>(reader: R, options: ReadOptions) -> Result<PackageSummary, XlsxReadError>` —
  discovers ZIP/OOXML parts (workbook, worksheets, styles, shared strings,
  external links, macros) under the same resource budget as a full read,
  without interpreting workbook semantics.
- `open_xlsx_document_path`, `open_xlsx_document_bytes`, and
  `open_xlsx_document<R: Read + Seek + Send + 'static>` return an
  `XlsxDocument` under the `OpenOptions`/`ReadLimits` budget. The document
  retains no host path and exposes no ZIP or XML types.
- `ReadOptions::default()` / `ReadOptions::new(ReadLimits)`, `.limits()`
- `ReadLimits::default()` + 27 `.with_max_*(u64) -> Result<Self, ReadOptionsError>` budgets:
  archive bytes, ZIP entry count, per-entry/total uncompressed bytes,
  compression ratio, XML depth/attributes, sheet count, cells per
  sheet/total, shared string count/bytes/total bytes, defined names,
  formula bytes per-cell/total, merged-range declarations, tables,
  table columns, table name bytes, per-table filter declarations, per-table
  filter/sort attribute text, plus phonetic runs, annotated references, and
  phonetic text bytes. Exceeding the merged-range or table budgets fails the
  read with the dedicated `XlsxErrorCode` variants `TooManyMergedRanges`,
  `TooManyTables`, `TooManyTableColumns`, `TableNameTooLarge`,
  `TooManyTableFilterItems`, or `TableFilterTextTooLarge`.

### Workbook model — read-only, format-neutral

- `WorkbookSnapshot`: `.sheets() -> &[Sheet]`, `.sheet_by_id(SheetId)`,
  `.sheet_by_name(&str)`, `.table(&str) -> Option<&Table>` (workbook-global
  `displayName`, case-insensitive), `.table_by_id(TableId)`,
  `.table_column_by_id(TableId, TableColumnId)`,
  `.table_column(TableId, &str)` (case-insensitive column name),
  `.containing_table(SheetId, CellAddress)` (unique containing table),
  `.defined_names()`, `.diagnostics()`, `.date_system()`,
  `.calculation_hints()`, `.source()`, `.provenance()`.
- `Sheet`: `.id()`, `.name() -> &SheetName`, `.visibility()`,
  `.cell(CellAddress) -> Option<&Cell>`, `.cell_by_a1(&str)`,
  `.cells()` (row-major order), `.len()`, `.is_empty()`, `.used_range()`,
  `.merged_ranges() -> &[CellRange]` (sorted by top-left address),
  `.tables() -> &[Table]` (XLSX declaration order).
- `Table`: `.id() -> TableId` (OOXML-valid non-zero, workbook-global stable ID),
  `.name() -> &TableName` (worksheet-local programmatic name),
  `.display_name() -> &TableName` (workbook-global formula/UI name),
  `.range()`, `.table_type()`, `.header_row_count()`, `.totals_row_count()`,
  `.totals_row_shown()`, `.columns() -> &[TableColumn]`, `.auto_filter()`,
  `.sort_state()`, `.style_info()`, and `.has_opaque_metadata()`.
- `TableColumn`: `.id() -> u32` (the original scalar API),
  `.column_id() -> TableColumnId` (typed non-zero stable identity),
  `.name()`, `.totals_row_function() -> Option<TotalsRowFunction>`,
  `.totals_row_label()`, `.calculated_column_formula()`, and
  `.totals_row_formula()`.
- `TableName` validates a table's formula/UI identity; `TableColumnName`
  validates a rename target and rejects a leading or trailing ASCII space
  because OOXML normalization would change that identity.
- `TableType` (`Worksheet | Xml | QueryTable`) exposes `.as_str()`.
  `TableFormula` exposes validated storage-form `.text()` and `.is_array()`.
  `TableAutoFilter` exposes its effective `.range()`,
  `.declared_range() -> Option<CellRange>` (absent when `autoFilter@ref` was
  omitted and inherited from the table), typed `.filter_columns()`, and an
  optional nested `.sort_state()`. Each `TableFilterColumn` exposes its zero-based
  `.column_id()`, button flags, and optional `TableFilterCriteria`
  (`Values | Custom | Dynamic | Color | Icon | Top`). `TableSortState`
  exposes `.range()`, `.case_sensitive()`, `.column_sort()`,
  `.sort_method()`, and typed `.conditions()`.
  Calendar, grouping, comparison, dynamic-filter, icon-set, sort-by, and
  sort-method tokens are exposed as non-exhaustive enums. Dynamic filters
  retain numeric `val`/`maxVal` through validated `TableNumericValue` source
  spellings and ISO `valIso`/`maxValIso` through validated
  `TableDateTimeValue` spellings. Strict SpreadsheetML rejects `maxVal`;
  Transitional SpreadsheetML may retain both serial and ISO forms.
  `TableStyleInfo` exposes its optional name plus the four first/last-column
  and row/column-stripe flags.
- `TotalsRowFunction` (`#[non_exhaustive]`): `Sum | Min | Max | Average |
  Count | CountNumbers | StdDev | Var | Custom`; `.as_str()` returns the
  OOXML token. Invalid table definitions, duplicate IDs or display names,
  worksheet-local duplicate programmatic names, and defined-name conflicts
  are reported as `xlsx.table.*` warning diagnostics and drop only that
  table. A later table whose range overlaps an already accepted table is
  likewise dropped with `xlsx.table.overlap`; merged-range problems use
  `xlsx.merged_range.*`.
- `Cell`: `.address()`, `.content() -> &CellContent`, `.number_format()`.
- `CellContent::Literal(CellValue) | Formula(FormulaCell)`.
- `CellValue` (`#[non_exhaustive]`): `Blank | Number(FiniteNumber) | Text(String) | Logical(bool) | Error(ExcelError)`.
- `CellAddress`: `::from_a1(&str)`, `::from_indices(row, column)`, `.row()`,
  `.column()`; `Display` renders `"A1"` style.
- `Row` / `Column`: 1-based, validated against `1..=1_048_576` /
  `1..=16_384` (`EXCEL_MAX_ROWS` / `EXCEL_MAX_COLUMNS`).
- `CellRange::new(start, end)`, `.start()`, `.end()`, `.height()`, `.width()`,
  `.contains(CellAddress)`.
- `FiniteNumber::new(f64)` — rejects NaN/±infinity; required wrapper for
  every numeric cell value and numeric option (e.g. `TODAY()`/`NOW()` serials).
- `SheetId`, `SheetName`, `SheetVisibility` (`Visible | Hidden | VeryHidden`),
  `DateSystem` (`Excel1900 | Excel1904`), `CalculationMode`,
  `CalculationHints`; calculation hints expose mode, calculation ID, host
  recalculation flags, and the optional iterative-calculation declaration.
  `CalculationHints::with_iterative_calculation(...)` sets that declaration.
  `WorkbookSource` / `WorkbookSourceKind`.
- `DefinedName`: `.name()`, `.scope()` (`DefinedNameScope::Workbook | Sheet(SheetId)`),
  `.formula() -> &FormulaText`, `.hidden()`.

### Defined-name inspection

- `analyze_defined_name(&WorkbookSnapshot, name, current_sheet)` uses default
  bounded options. `analyze_defined_name_with_options(...)` accepts
  `DefinedNameAnalysisOptions`, and `analyze_defined_name_cancellable(...)`
  additionally accepts a request-owned `CancellationToken`.
- `DefinedNameAnalysis` distinguishes `Rectangular`, `ThreeDimensional`,
  ordered `NonRectangular` areas, `EmptyReference`, `DynamicFormula`,
  `Constant`, typed `ExternalReference`, `Invalid`, `Unsupported`, and
  `NotFound`. Sheet spans and area order/multiplicity are preserved.
- `DefinedNameAnalysisOptions::new(CalculationOptions)` reuses formula,
  reference-area, and pairwise-work limits and adds configurable
  name-chain-depth and cumulative scan-node limits.
- Execution failures are separate from semantic results:
  `DefinedNameAnalysisError` reports `UnknownCurrentSheet`,
  `ResourceLimit`, or `Cancelled`, with a typed
  `DefinedNameAnalysisLimitKind` when a budget was exhausted.

### Package-backed document and preservation writing

- `XlsxDocument`: `.workbook()`, `.input_hash()`, `.kind()`,
  `.semantic_revision()`, `.presentation()`, `.presentation_revision()`,
  `.package_summary()`, `.workbook_part()`, `.worksheet_part(SheetId)`, and
  `.table_part(TableId)`.
- `XlsxDocumentKind`: `Xlsx | Xlsm`. Macro parts are retained but never
  executed.
- `write_preserved_xlsx_bytes(&XlsxDocument, WriteOptions) ->
  Result<Vec<u8>, XlsxWriteError>` raw-copies every unchanged ZIP entry.
- Accepted table metadata participates in write verification. Unchanged
  source-linked table parts are retained byte-for-byte. Stable-ID table
  authoring patches only modeled SpreadsheetML children and attributes in the
  accepted table part; foreign namespace and opaque extension content is
  preserved. The canonical serializer emits modeled worksheet tables and
  fails with `UnsupportedPreservation` rather than discard opaque metadata or
  invent the dependent parts required by query/XML tables, differential
  formats, or custom table styles. Canonical serialization also enforces the
  complete OOXML table-name and column-name rules even though the older public
  constructors retain their 0.1.8 validation contract for patch-version
  compatibility.
- `write_recalculated_xlsx_bytes(&XlsxDocument, &CalculationSnapshot,
  RecalculationWriteOptions) -> Result<RecalculatedWorkbook,
  XlsxWriteError>` prepares owned verified bytes plus a `WriteReport`.
- `write_recalculated_xlsx(&XlsxDocument, &CalculationSnapshot, &mut impl
  Write, RecalculationWriteOptions) -> Result<WriteReport, XlsxWriteError>`
  prepares and verifies all bytes before touching the writer.
- `write_recalculated_xlsx_path(...) -> Result<WriteReport,
  XlsxWriteError>` uses a sibling temporary file and refuses existing
  destinations unless `WriteOptions::with_replace_existing(true)` is set.
- `RecalculationWritePolicy`: `RequireComplete` (default) or
  `InvalidateUnavailable`. Invalidation removes stale caches, requests host
  recalculation, and records every affected cell and diagnostic.
- `WriteReport`: `.is_complete()`, `.policy()`, `.materialized_count()`,
  `.invalidated_cells()`, `.changed_parts()`, `.removed_parts()`,
  `.diagnostics()`, and `.provenance()`.
- `RecalculatedWorkbook`: `.bytes()`, `.into_bytes()`, `.report()`,
  `.into_parts()`, and `.save_path(...)`.
- With the optional `capability-fs` feature,
  `RecalculatedWorkbook::save_in_directory(&cap_std::fs::Dir, file_name,
  WriteOptions)` installs beneath an already-open directory identity. The
  destination must be one relative file name; this is the primitive used by
  the MCP Save As boundary.
- `WriteOptions::default()` refuses implicit destination replacement.
  `WriteLimits` owns output, entry, XML, edit, result, relationship, temporary
  storage, and verification budgets.
- Branch on `XlsxWriteError::code()` /
  `XlsxWriteErrorCode::as_str()`, never on human-readable messages.

### Workbook authoring and typed edits

- `WorkbookDraft::new()` starts with visible `Sheet1`;
  `WorkbookDraft::from_document(&XlsxDocument)` retains the exact source
  package privately.
- `.workbook()`, `.presentation()`, `.semantic_revision()`,
  `.presentation_revision()`, `.is_document_backed()`.
- `.set_cell_value(...)`, `.set_cell_formula(...)`,
  `.set_cell_dynamic_formula(..., Option<CellRange>)`, `.clear_cell(...)`,
  `.set_cell_number_format(...)`.
- `.set_annotated_text(...)`, `.set_phonetics(...)`, `.clear_phonetics(...)`,
  `.set_frozen_pane(...)`, `.clear_frozen_pane(...)`.
- `.add_sheet(...)`, `.rename_sheet(...)`, `.set_sheet_visibility(...)`.
- `.set_defined_name(...)`, `.remove_defined_name(...)`,
  `.set_date_system(...)`, `.set_calculation_hints(...)`.
- `NumberFormat::built_in(...)` and `NumberFormat::custom(...)` validate the
  built-in/custom ID boundary. `NumberFormatKind` distinguishes general,
  numeric, date, time, date-time, and duration interpretation. Custom formats
  require a nonempty code.
- `write_xlsx_draft_bytes`, `write_xlsx_draft`, and
  `write_xlsx_draft_path` require a `CalculationSnapshot` produced from the
  current `draft.workbook()`. New drafts produce deterministic canonical
  XLSX; document drafts preserve unrelated XLSX/XLSM parts.
- Dynamic formulas can be authored in canonical drafts. Existing
  document-backed dynamic formulas can be recalculated and cache-rewritten,
  but adding or replacing one through a document draft fails with
  `UnsupportedPreservation` until source metadata-index merging is available.

### XLSX presentation

- `DocumentPresentation`: `.revision()`, `.diagnostics()`,
  `.frozen_pane(SheetId)`, `.worksheet_phonetic_properties(SheetId)`,
  `.row_phonetic_visibility(SheetId, Row)`,
  `.column_phonetic_visibility(SheetId)`,
  `.cell_phonetics(SheetId, CellAddress)`, and
  `.phonetic_cell_entries(SheetId) -> impl Iterator<Item = (CellAddress, CellPhonetics)>`.
  The iterator yields only cells carrying at least one run, in row-major
  address order, reporting the same visibility `cell_phonetics` reports for the
  same address. A cell whose annotation holds only `phoneticPr` display
  properties without `rPh` runs — common in Japanese workbooks — is skipped by
  the iterator and stays reachable through `cell_phonetics`.
- `CellPhonetics`: `.runs()`, `.properties()`,
  `.explicit_cell_visibility()`, `.explicit_row_visibility()`,
  `.explicit_column_visibility()`, `.effective_visibility()`, and
  `.resolved_runs(&str) -> Result<Vec<ResolvedPhoneticRun>, ValidationError>`.
- `ResolvedPhoneticRun`: `.base_bytes() -> Range<usize>`, `.base_slice()`,
  `.text()`, `.run()`. `resolved_runs` translates each run's range from the
  UTF-16 code units XLSX stores into the byte offsets Rust indexes with, and
  rejects a range that splits a surrogate pair or runs past the base text with
  the existing `ValidationError`. Presentation state does not hold cell text,
  so the base text comes from the workbook snapshot: look the address up with
  `WorkbookSnapshot::sheet_by_id(..).cell(address)` and match
  `CellContent::Literal(CellValue::Text(..))`. The returned value keeps that
  exact borrow, so a byte range cannot be paired with another cell's string.
- `PhoneticTextRange::new(start_utf16, end_utf16)`, `.start_utf16()`,
  `.end_utf16()`; when a range is validated against its base text, a boundary
  cannot split a surrogate pair.
- `PhoneticRun::new(range, text)`, `.base_range()`, `.text()`.
- `PhoneticProperties::new(font_id)`, `.font_id()`,
  `.effective_font_id()`, `.phonetic_type()`, `.alignment()`,
  `.with_phonetic_type(...)`, `.with_alignment(...)`.
- `PhoneticType`: `FullWidthKatakana | HalfWidthKatakana | Hiragana |
  NoConversion`; `PhoneticAlignment`: `NoControl | Left | Center |
  Distributed`.
- `ColumnPhoneticVisibility` records one column range and whether phonetics
  are shown for it.
- `PhoneticWriteOptions::show()` / `hide()` / `new(bool)`,
  `.with_properties(...)`.
- `FrozenPane::new(frozen_rows, frozen_columns)`, `.frozen_rows()`,
  `.frozen_columns()`, `.is_clear()`.
- Canonical authoring supports default font record `0`; source rich-text
  phonetic edits and right-to-left frozen-pane edits fail closed with
  `UnsupportedPreservation`.

### Atomic batches and persistent recalculation sessions

- `WorkbookChange` is the non-exhaustive typed mutation union. Construct
  changes with `set_cell_value`, `set_cell_formula`,
  `set_cell_dynamic_formula`, `clear_cell`, `set_cell_number_format`,
  `add_sheet`, `rename_sheet`, `set_sheet_visibility`, `set_defined_name`,
  `remove_defined_name`, `set_date_system`, `set_calculation_hints`,
  `rename_table(TableId, TableName)`,
  `rename_table_column(TableId, TableColumnId, TableColumnName)`, and
  `resize_table_rows(TableId, first_data_row, last_data_row)`.
- `EditBatch::new(changes)` preserves operation order.
  `WorkbookDraft::apply_changes(batch)` stages once and commits one semantic
  revision or rolls the complete batch back. If every accepted operation is
  a semantic no-op, the receipt keeps the base revision and reports no
  topology or calculation-metadata change.
- Table and column renames rewrite every typed reference in worksheet cells,
  defined names, calculated-column formulas, and totals-row formulas while
  preserving source text outside the target spans. Row resize keeps stable
  table/column identities, remaps filter/sort ranges, materializes modeled
  calculated/totals/header cells, and can expand a header-only empty table.
  Unsupported metadata, collisions, formula rewrite failures, limits, and
  cancellation roll back the complete batch.
- `WorkbookCalculationSession::new(draft)` / `::create()` owns the mutable
  draft plus persistent parsed formulas, dependency state, results, dirty
  roots, and bounded delta history.
- `session.apply_changes(expected_revision, batch)` returns `EditReceipt`;
  it distinguishes all source/format changes from calculation-semantic
  changes, reports stable `.changed_table_ids()`, and records
  topology/metadata impact. Stale writers fail with
  `SessionErrorCode::RevisionMismatch`.
- To validate and size an edit before committing it, call
  `session.prepare_changes(expected_revision, batch)`. The returned
  `PreparedEditBatch` exposes the prospective `.workbook()` and `.receipt()`;
  `session.install_changes(prepared)` commits only if its base revision is
  still current. `prepare_changes_cancellable` adds cooperative cancellation
  to formula rewriting, table materialization, and final snapshot/index
  construction.
- `session.recalculate(RecalculationMode::Auto, options, token)` returns a
  `CalculationDelta`. `Auto` uses a proven dirty subset and falls back to
  full calculation for formula/name/sheet/options or uncertain dynamic/spill
  topology. Forced `Incremental` fails closed when unsafe.
- For work outside a session lock, call `prepare_recalculation`, run the
  returned `PreparedCalculation`, then call `install`. `CancellationToken`
  provides cooperative cancellation. Running a prepared calculation returns
  `CompletedCalculation`; cancellation or a newer workbook revision never
  replaces the installed current result.
- `CalculationDelta` distinguishes dirty, evaluated, changed, and removed
  materialized cells. `CalculationDeltaCell` carries each changed cell,
  materialization origin, and result. `CalculationExecutionMode` reports
  `Incremental | Full`, while non-exhaustive `CalculationDecisionReason`
  explains why that schedule was selected. `changes_since(cursor, limit)`
  returns a bounded `CalculationDeltaPage`.
- `SessionLimits` bounds batch operations, evaluated formulas, delta cells,
  retained deltas, page size, cumulative formula-rewrite formula/source/AST/
  source-edit work, and table-resize materialized cells. `SessionErrorCode`
  is the stable machine-readable error family.
- `ApplyChangesError` distinguishes a staged `ValidationError` from a
  `SessionError`. `SessionError` exposes `.code()`, `.message()`, and
  `.detail()`.

### Formula storage — independent of calculation

- `FormulaCell`: `.dialect()`, `.text() -> Option<&FormulaText>`,
  `.saved_result() -> &SavedResult`, `.metadata() -> &FormulaMetadata`,
  `.recalculate_always()`.
- `FormulaText::from_xlsx(String)` / `::from_user_input(String)`, `.as_str()`.
- `SavedResult`: `Missing | Present(CellValue) | Invalid(SavedResultIssue)` —
  the value the *file itself* cached. `calculate_workbook` never reads or
  writes this; it is a separate, independent fact about the source.
- `FormulaMetadata` (`#[non_exhaustive]`): `Normal | Shared{..} | Array{..} | DynamicArray{..} | DataTable{..}`.
- `SharedFormulaRole`: `Anchor | Follower { anchor }`.
- `FormulaDialect` (`#[non_exhaustive]`): currently only `ExcelA1`.

### Capability inventory — optional

- `scan_formula_capabilities(&WorkbookSnapshot) -> FormulaCapabilityReport`
- `scan_formula_capabilities_with_options(&WorkbookSnapshot, CalculationOptions) -> FormulaCapabilityReport` —
  use this (with the same `CalculationLimits` you'll pass to
  `calculate_workbook`) to align static parse, name, and dependency budgets.
  Evaluation-only limits such as materialized array cells, calculated text
  bytes, and data-dependent iterations can still surface during calculation.
- `FormulaCapabilityReport`: `.entries()`, `.formula_count()`,
  `.supported_count()`, `.unsupported_count()`, `.is_supported()`.
- `FormulaCapabilityEntry`: `.cell()` and `.capability()`.
- `FormulaCapability`: `Supported | Unsupported(Vec<CalculationIssue>)`.
- The inventory is static: it does not calculate values, inspect saved values,
  or change what `calculate_workbook` returns. Use it for bulk migration
  planning, support dashboards, or user interfaces that need a formula-surface
  inventory. Normal workbook calculation does not require it.

### Function catalog and workbook demand

- `supported_function_catalog() -> Vec<FunctionCatalogEntry>` returns the
  deterministic accepted-name catalog for this build. Each entry exposes
  `.name()`, `.canonical_name()`, `.is_alias()`, `.returns_array()`, and
  `.is_official()`. The current catalog contains 412 official Excel-facing
  names and one non-official compatibility entry for the OOXML dummy-function
  marker, for 413 accepted entries. The versioned 0.1.14 catalog remains
  386 official names and 387 accepted entries byte-exact.
- The 19 official names added in 0.1.14 are `CONVERT`, `BESSELI`, `BESSELJ`,
  `BESSELK`, `BESSELY`, `COMPLEX`, `IMABS`, `IMAGINARY`, `IMARGUMENT`,
  `IMCONJUGATE`, `IMREAL`, `IMDIV`, `IMPOWER`, `IMPRODUCT`, `IMSUB`, `IMSUM`,
  `IMEXP`, `IMLN`, and `IMSQRT`. None returns an array.
- The 26 official fixed-income names added on top of 0.1.14 are `ACCRINT`,
  `ACCRINTM`, `COUPDAYBS`, `COUPDAYS`, `COUPDAYSNC`, `COUPNCD`, `COUPNUM`,
  `COUPPCD`, `DISC`, `DURATION`, `INTRATE`, `MDURATION`, `ODDFPRICE`,
  `ODDFYIELD`, `ODDLPRICE`, `ODDLYIELD`, `PRICE`, `PRICEDISC`, `PRICEMAT`,
  `RECEIVED`, `TBILLEQ`, `TBILLPRICE`, `TBILLYIELD`, `YIELD`, `YIELDDISC`,
  and `YIELDMAT`. None returns an array.
- Fixed-income day counts cover US 30/360, Actual/Actual, Actual/360,
  Actual/365, and European 30/360; coupon schedules walk backward from
  maturity and preserve month-end policy. `YIELD(N>1)` and `ODDFYIELD` share
  a safeguarded Newton/bracket root solver bounded to 100 evaluations in
  Excel-compatible mode, charging the calculation budget and observing
  cancellation per evaluation.
- `CONVERT` uses a case-sensitive typed unit registry with explicit decimal and
  binary prefix policies. Complex functions share one finite internal value,
  parser, suffix policy, canonical text formatter, and scaled arithmetic.
  Bessel J/Y and I/K use separate first-party numerical families; their
  iterative work consumes the calculation budget and observes cancellation.
- All four families share one first-party special-function foundation: a
  Lanczos `ln_gamma`, regularized incomplete gamma and beta kernels, and a
  safeguarded inverse solver. A family's cumulative and quantile forms are
  evaluated through the same tail kernel; the density forms are built on the
  same primitives.
- The inverse solver brackets and then refines with alternating bisection and
  secant steps, and charges the calculation budget for every step. A search
  that cannot converge returns `#N/A` from `GAMMA.INV` and `BETA.INV`, which is
  the error Microsoft documents; it never returns an unconverged number.
- `BINOM.INV` and `CRITBINOM` bisect over the integer support instead, and
  verify `CDF(k-1) < alpha <= CDF(k)` against regularized incomplete-beta CDF
  evaluations before returning. Full-support and degenerate CDFs resolve exactly
  without enumerating the support; paths that require exact integer indexing
  reject support indices above `2^53` instead of using a lossy conversion.
  Binomial and negative-binomial mass complements use `ln1p(-p)` so tiny
  probabilities survive exponentiation over large counts.
- `HYPGEOM.DIST` and `HYPGEOMDIST` evaluate sample sizes through 10,000 as a
  falling-factorial product that never differences two large `lnGamma` values,
  which is what keeps very large populations accurate.
- `scan_function_usage(&WorkbookSnapshot) -> FunctionUsageReport` and
  `scan_function_usage_with_options(&WorkbookSnapshot, CalculationOptions)`
  count normalized function calls without calculating the workbook.
- `FunctionUsageEntry` exposes `.name()`, `.support()`, `.call_count()`,
  `.formula_count()`, and up to eight deterministic `.sample_cells()`.
  `FunctionUsageReport` also records parsed and unparsed formula counts.
- `FunctionSupport`: `Supported | Unsupported`; it is independent from
  whether a particular call later produces an Excel error value.

### Calculation

- `calculate_workbook(&WorkbookSnapshot, CalculationOptions) -> CalculationSnapshot` —
  stateless full recalculation and the correctness oracle; never mutates the
  source snapshot.
- `CalculationOptions::default().with_today_serial(FiniteNumber).with_now_serial(FiniteNumber).with_limits(CalculationLimits).with_arithmetic_semantics(ArithmeticSemantics).with_financial_solver_semantics(FinancialSolverSemantics)` —
  `TODAY()` and `NOW()` never read the host clock. Omitting the corresponding
  serial makes that formula report `VolatileInputMissing`.
- **Two numeric-compatibility axes, both defaulting to Excel's behavior rather
  than to what 0.1.2 did.** `ArithmeticSemantics`: `ExcelNearZero` (default)
  applies Excel's narrow correction only when the exact decimal/rational trace
  is zero and the binary residue is within `1e-15` of the cancelling operands'
  relative scale. Thus `=0.1+0.2-0.3` is `0`, while
  `=100.1-100-0.1` retains `-5.689893001203927e-15`, matching the committed
  Excel saved cache. `Ieee754` leaves every residue. The correction reaches
  the operator path, the array path, and the running totals behind `SUM`,
  `AVERAGE`, `SUMIF(S)`, `AVERAGEIF(S)`, `SUBTOTAL`, `SUMPRODUCT`, and `NPV`,
  so those cannot disagree with each other.
  `FinancialSolverSemantics`: `ExcelIterationBudget` (default) applies
  Microsoft's per-function budget — 20 iterations/`1e-7` for `IRR` and `RATE`,
  100/`1e-8` for `XIRR` — so inputs Excel abandons yield `#NUM!` here too;
  `ExtendedSearch` searches longer, as 0.1.2 did. **Upgrading from 0.1.2
  changes calculated numbers unless you select `ArithmeticSemantics::Ieee754`
  and `FinancialSolverSemantics::ExtendedSearch`.** Both axes are also carried
  by the interop DTO and the Python, Node.js, and MCP boundaries.
  `docs/NUMERICS.md` records the policies and their oracles.
- `CalculationLimits::default()` + 12 `.with_max_*(u64) -> Result<Self, CalculationOptionsError>`
  budgets: formula tokens, source bytes, AST nodes, AST nesting depth,
  dependency edges, reference areas, array cells, calculated text bytes,
  data-dependent function iterations, LET bindings, active LAMBDA depth, and
  cumulative LAMBDA/MAP invocations.
- `LAMBDA` is a first-class scoped value. Literal, immediate, `LET`-bound,
  workbook-defined, and sheet-local callables share one evaluator with lexical
  capture and caller isolation. `MAP`, `BYROW`, `BYCOL`, `REDUCE`, `SCAN`,
  `MAKEARRAY`, and `ISOMITTED` consume the same typed callable representation;
  final callable results are `#CALC!`, while attempts to use a callable as a
  scalar operand are `#VALUE!`.
- `CalculationSnapshot`: `.cell(CalculationCellId) -> Option<&CalculationCellResult>`,
  `.cells()`, `.materialized_cell(CalculationCellId)`,
  `.materialized_cells()`, `.len()`, `.is_empty()`, `.options()`,
  `.provenance()`.
- `MaterializedCalculationCell` carries `.origin()` and `.result()`.
  `MaterializedResultOrigin` distinguishes a direct formula cell, a cell in
  a legacy-array region, and a cell in a dynamic-spill region; array origins
  carry their anchor and complete result range.
- `CalculationCellId::new(SheetId, CellAddress)`.
- `CalculationCellResult`: `Value(CellValue) | Unavailable(CalculationIssue)`.
- `INDEX(reference, 0, column)` returns the selected complete column,
  `INDEX(reference, row, 0)` returns the selected complete row, and zero for
  both indexes returns the complete reference. Scalar formulas apply legacy
  implicit intersection; array contexts materialize the selected rectangle.
- Unary and binary array operators containing whole-column references resolve
  one common row extent from the greatest populated row among the columns
  those operands reference, with a one-row minimum on an otherwise empty
  sheet. Cells in other columns of the same sheet do not widen it, so the
  value depends only on the cells the expression's dependency rectangles
  cover and a full and an incremental recalculation agree. Unpopulated cells
  in that extent are `Blank`; directly resolved source arrays and operator
  outputs are charged cumulatively to `max_array_cells`. Function calls retain
  function-defined argument boundaries: each array argument has an
  independent bounded evaluation context, and a function return does not
  establish a whole-column operator extent by itself. If another direct
  whole-column operand establishes an enclosing context, the returned array
  is charged to that context before the operator consumes it.
- Direct 3-D references are supported for `SUM`, `AVERAGE`, `AVERAGEA`,
  `COUNT`, `COUNTA`, `MAX`, `MAXA`, `MIN`, `MINA`, `PRODUCT`, `STDEV.P`,
  `STDEV.S`, `VAR.P`, and `VAR.S`, including catalogued legacy aliases.
  Workbook tab order defines the inclusive span, including hidden sheets;
  reversing the written endpoints does not change the participating sheets.
  Direct 3-D arguments to `INDEX` and `VLOOKUP` produce `#VALUE!`, and
  `OFFSET` produces `#REF!`. Other direct consumers report
  `UnsupportedSheetRange`. Bare 3-D references and 3-D references composed
  through array operators produce `#VALUE!`; an enclosing aggregate does not
  widen that nested context. The scanner and evaluator use the same policy.
  Incremental dependency state stores each 3-D input as one compact
  rectangle span rather than one rectangle per sheet, so compiled size grows
  with the number of references, not with the number of sheets spanned. The
  span is expanded only while building graph edges, and
  `max_dependency_edges` still counts the distinct edges produced.
- Structured table references (`Table1[Amount]`, `[@Amount]`, item selectors,
  column spans, and nested/escaped column spellings) are typed and resolved
  against stable table/column identities. Empty data or totals bands remain a
  valid empty reference, while `#This Row` uses the formula's actual table
  row. Dependencies retain table identity and topology, so table rename or
  resize forces a safe graph rebuild rather than reusing stale geometry.
- Reference union, intersection, and range operators preserve ordered
  multi-area identity. `AREAS` is in the official catalog; consumers that
  require one rectangle fail with the documented Excel error rather than
  silently flattening a multi-area value.
- Spill postfix references such as `A1#` and the OOXML storage form
  `_xlfn.ANCHORARRAY(A1)` share one typed node. Evaluation resolves the
  current spill registry, schedules the producer anchor first, rejects
  non-anchors, propagates blocked spills, and removes stale spill children
  when a shape changes.
- External-workbook references and sheet-qualified defined names are typed by
  the parser. External workbook calculation remains unsupported and never
  opens or follows the referenced package.

### Diagnostics and provenance

- `DiagnosticSeverity`: `Info | Warning | Error`.
- `SourceLocation::source`, `::sheet`, and `::cell` construct source-linked
  locations; `.with_byte_offset(...)` adds a zero-based byte offset.
- `Provenance` pairs a `ProviderIdentity` with an optional `InputHash`.
- `WriteProvenance` records the input hash, semantic and presentation
  revisions, calculator identity, and deterministic calculation options used
  by a completed write.

## Error taxonomy — pick the right one, never mix

| Type | Means | Result exists? | Machine check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ValidationError` | Caller-supplied address/name/number/model value violates an invariant | No object is produced | `.code(): ValidationErrorCode`; match on the non-exhaustive enum only when structured fields are needed |
| `ReadOptionsError` | A `ReadLimits` budget was invalid (zero) | Fails before reading starts | Match on the enum variant |
| `CalculationOptionsError` | A `CalculationLimits` budget was invalid (zero) | Fails before calculation starts | Match on the enum variant |
| `DefinedNameAnalysisOptionsError` | A defined-name chain or scan budget was invalid (zero) | Fails before inspection starts | Match the concrete error type |
| `DefinedNameAnalysisError` | Defined-name inspection saw an unknown current sheet, exhausted a budget, or was cancelled | No semantic inspection result is produced | `.kind()`, optional `.limit()`, and `.detail()` |
| `XlsxReadError` | No trustworthy `WorkbookSnapshot` could be produced at all | No snapshot | `.code(): XlsxErrorCode`, `.source_id()`, `.detail()` |
| `WriteOptionsError` | A `WriteLimits` budget was invalid (zero) | Fails before writing starts | Match on the enum variant |
| `XlsxWriteError` | The source/calculation binding, package plan, write budget, destination, or completed output was invalid | No successful output artifact | `.code(): XlsxWriteErrorCode`, `.source_id()`, `.detail()` |
| `ApplyChangesError` | An atomic session edit failed either session-state or workbook validation | No edit is committed | Match `Session` or `Validation` |
| `SessionError` | Revision, incremental-safety, cancellation, cursor, or session resource rules rejected an operation | Session remains valid; installation is rejected when applicable | `.code(): SessionErrorCode`, `.detail()` |
| `Diagnostic` | Read succeeded, but a compatibility caveat exists (e.g. external link, macro) | Snapshot exists, on `.diagnostics()` | `.code(): DiagnosticCode`, `.severity()`, `.location()` |
| `CalculationIssue` | One specific formula could not be calculated | Independent formulas can still produce results; dependents may report `BlockedByUpstream` | `.code(): CalculationIssueCode`, `.detail()` |
| `CellValue::Error(ExcelError)` | An actual spreadsheet error value (`#DIV/0!`, `#REF!`, ...) | This *is* the cell's value | `.as_str()` on the `ExcelError` |

An unsupported engine capability is never converted into an `ExcelError` and
can never be hidden by a spreadsheet-side `IFERROR`/`IFNA` — it always
surfaces as a `CalculationIssue`, which is a Rust-level fact about the
engine, not a spreadsheet-level fact about the data.

## Scope / non-goals

CellRune supports ordinary Transitional SpreadsheetML workbooks and a scoped
set of Excel formula syntax and functions. Unsupported formulas appear as
structured per-cell calculation issues while independent formulas continue to
calculate. Out of scope for the current version:

- `.xls`, `.xlsb`, `.ods`, and CSV.
- Macro, add-in, external-workbook, query, or data-connection execution.
- 3-D references outside the audited direct-consumer policy described under
  Calculation, and data-table calculation.
- Iterative calculation and automatic host-time or random inputs (`TODAY()`
  and `NOW()` are supported only through explicit `CalculationOptions` inputs).

## Development verification

- `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` runs the standard Rust test
  suite.
- `conformance/README.md` documents the Excel-saved and Apache POI fixture
  layout, focused audit command, classifications, maintenance policy, and
  optional local corpus tests.

## Runnable examples

The repository path is `crates/cellrune/examples/`; the published crate
package path is `examples/`. From the repository root use
`cargo run -p cellrune --example <name> -- [arguments]`. From an extracted
crate package use `cargo run --example <name> -- [arguments]`.

- `read_only_inspection.rs` — read a workbook and inspect cells/diagnostics
  without ever calling `calculate_workbook`.
- `capability_scan_only.rs` — build an optional static formula-capability
  inventory and inspect `FormulaCapability`.
- `handle_read_error.rs` — match on `XlsxErrorCode` for a deliberately
  invalid input; the stable-code contract, concretely.
- `compare_saved_vs_calculated.rs` — reads a formula's `SavedResult` and a
  fresh `calculate_workbook` result side by side, demonstrating that neither
  operation touches the other.
- `read_and_calculate.rs` — the full pipeline against a real file (takes a
  path argument); also prints per-issue diagnostics for a whole workbook.
- `create_and_write.rs` — creates, calculates, and writes a canonical workbook
  (optional destination path argument).
- `recalculate_and_save.rs` — opens an XLSX/XLSM package, recalculates it, and
  performs verified Save As (input and output path arguments).
- `dynamic_array_write.rs` — authors, calculates, and writes a canonical
  `FILTER` spill (optional destination path argument).
- `inspect_phonetic_workbook.rs` — prints frozen-pane metadata and, for each
  annotated cell, the byte range and base slice each run covers; shows the
  `phonetic_cell_entries` → workbook base text → `resolved_runs` join a
  consumer needs (input path argument).
- `write_phonetic_workbook.rs` — authors annotated text and a frozen pane
  (output path argument).
- `select_calculation_modes.rs` — calculates the same formulas under the
  default Excel-compatible policies and under the 0.1.2 opt-ins, so the numbers
  `ArithmeticSemantics` and `FinancialSolverSemantics` change are visible side
  by side (no arguments).
